newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy still on recovery track - BOJ quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy still on recovery track - BOJ quoted.

text.p: Japan's economy is still on a gradual recovery track, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita was quoted as saying on Friday.
"The overall economy is still in the process of gradually recovering," Matsushita was quoted as saying by Economic Planning Agency Minister Shusei Tanaka.

Matsushita said that according to the BOJ's quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment for August, some companies had become cautious about the business environment due to problems with inventory adjustment, but capital investment plans had been revised upward.
This showed that business sentiment was likely to improve in the coming months.
Matsushita said short-term market interest rates had been fluctuating but had remained generally below the official discount rate of 0.5 percent.

The interest rate on three-month certificates of deposit had gradually declined to around 0.5 percent from around the 0.6 percent level in early August, Matsushita told a meeting of economic ministers.

After declining since mid-July, long-term market interest rates had settled at around 3.0 percent. Stock prices had recovered to the 21,000 level on the Nikkei stock market index in August but had started falling again.
Meanwhile, the yen had turned slightly easier against the dollar to 108 yen in early August and had moved around the 108 yen level for a while.
The yen had weakened further since then and was now around the 109 yen level, the BOJ governor was quoted as saying by Tanaka at a news conference.
